title: Earth's velocity on 16 June 2023 21:22:39 UTC and gravitational focusing: the exact kinematic inputs for the LZ event
question: What are the exact observer velocity, v_max, delta_max and their uncertainties at the LZ event instant, and how do solar and terrestrial gravitational focusing alter the high-velocity tail, the inelastic rate and the Higgsino window?
headline_result: |v_E| = 265.74 +- 2.5 km/s at the event (0.2 km/s below all corpus models), delta_max(248 keV, 1 TeV) = 387.13 keV; solar focusing adds 1.10 km/s to v_max (delta_max 388.03 keV) and x1.04-1.16 to the inelastic rate at delta = 300-380 keV, with <= 1.3 % effect on the date evidence; delta_max >= 387 keV holds 9.8 % of the year.
